title: Trial Balance
description: Check whether your debits and credits are balanced.
html:
What is a trial balance?

A trial balance is a list of all general ledger accounts and their balances at a specific date.

Its main purpose is to check whether total debit balances equal total credit balances.

Total Debit Balances = Total Credit Balances

Example trial balance

Account
Debit
Credit
Cash
$15,000
—
Equipment
$10,000
—
Accounts Payable

$15,000

$25,000

Does a balanced trial balance mean everything is correct?

No.

A trial balance can still balance even when certain accounting errors exist.

Example of an error that still balances

Suppose a company buys Equipment for $3,000 cash, but accidentally debits Supplies instead of Equipment.

The debit is still $3,000 and the credit is still $3,000, so the trial balance can still balance.

But the wrong account was used.

Important

  • A trial balance checks debit and credit equality.
  • It is prepared from ledger balances.
  • A balanced trial balance does not guarantee no errors exist.
  • It is an important step before preparing financial statements.

quiz.prompt: If a trial balance has $42,000 of total debits, what should total credits equal?
quiz.explanation: For a balanced trial balance, total debit balances must equal total credit balances.

objectives: Explain trial balance and its underlying principles.
Apply the topic to a financial-reporting scenario.
